seoDescription: Explore the power of no-code AI agent teams with Flowise's new Agentflows feature. This tutorial guides you through building sophisticated multi-agent systems without writing any code, leveraging the underlying LangGraph framework. Learn to create a supervisor agent to orchestrate tasks and worker agents with specific roles. You'll build two practical projects: a complete software development team and a lead research team equipped with Google Search tools to perform real-time data gathering and analysis.

chapters.title: Introducing Flowise Agentflows
chapters.description: An overview of the new no-code AI agent team builder in Flowise, explaining supervisors, worker agents, and the projects to be built.

chapters.title: Setting Up the Supervisor Agent
chapters.description: Learn how to begin building a software development team by adding and configuring the supervisor agent and its associated Chat OpenAI model.

chapters.title: Configuring the LLM and First Worker Agent
chapters.description: This chapter covers connecting and configuring the Chat OpenAI GPT-4o model, then adding the first worker agent for the Product Designer role.

chapters.title: Defining Worker Roles and Inheritance
chapters.description: Learn about model inheritance for worker agents and create the first team member, the Product Designer, by defining its specific role in a prompt.

chapters.title: Initial Test with One Worker Agent
chapters.description: This chapter explains worker node settings like prompt variables and max iterations before testing the team with just the single Product Designer agent.

chapters.title: Building the Full Software Development Team
chapters.description: Add and configure the Developer and Technical Writer agents to complete the software development team, then run a full test to see them work in sequence.

chapters.title: Testing the Complete Software Team
chapters.description: Observe the full software development team in action as the supervisor orchestrates the product designer, developer, and technical writer to build an app.

chapters.title: Starting the Lead Research Team Project
chapters.description: Begin creating the second example, a lead research team that uses tools, by setting up the supervisor and defining the roles for the researcher and sales rep.

chapters.title: Defining Roles and the Need for Tools
chapters.description: This chapter defines the roles for the lead researcher and sales representative and explains why the researcher will need an external tool to access live web data.

chapters.title: Using Prompt Variables
chapters.description: Learn how to use curly braces as dynamic variables in prompts and populate them with specific information, such as a lead's name and company.

chapters.title: Testing the Team Without Search Tools
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to populate prompt variables for the lead research team and runs an initial test to show its output before adding a search tool.

chapters.title: Analyzing Pre-Tool Results and Integrating Google Search
chapters.description: Review the initial, data-limited results, then add the Google Custom Search tool to the researcher agent to enable live web access.

chapters.title: Configuring Google Custom Search Credentials
chapters.description: This chapter walks through the process of creating credentials for the Google Custom Search tool, including getting an API key and a Programmable Search Engine ID.

chapters.title: Final Test with the Search-Enabled Team
chapters.description: Run the lead research agent team again, this time with the Google Search tool enabled, and analyze how the agent uses the tool to gather up-to-date information.

summary:
## Introduction to Flowise Agentflows

**Agentflows** is a new feature in Flowise that allows you to build **no-code AI agent teams**. This enables the creation of sophisticated multi-agent systems by simply dragging and dropping nodes on a canvas. The system is built on the **LangGraph** framework.

Key components include:

*   **Supervisor Agent**: The team manager that receives the user's task, delegates sub-tasks to appropriate workers, and orchestrates the entire workflow until completion.
*   **Worker Agents**: Individual agents assigned specific roles, responsibilities, and sometimes tools to contribute to the overall goal.

## Project 1: Software Development Team

This project demonstrates building an agent team to simulate a software development process.

### Team Structure

1.  **Supervisor**: Orchestrates the workflow.
2.  **Product Designer**: Receives the user request and creates a detailed feature and design plan.
3.  **Developer**: Takes the design plan and writes the application code (e.g., using React, Next.js).
4.  **Technical Writer**: Creates a user manual in Markdown based on the final product.

> [!NOTE]
> The Supervisor agent intelligently determines the correct sequence of workers. For example, it will always run the Product Designer before the Developer, ensuring a logical workflow.

### Key Concepts

*   **Model Inheritance**: Worker agents can **inherit** the LLM used by the Supervisor. Alternatively, you can assign a unique LLM to each worker, which is useful for tasks like verification where different models check each other's work.
*   **Worker Prompts**: The core of a worker agent is its prompt, which clearly defines its name, role, responsibilities, and expected output format.

## Project 2: Lead Research Team with Tools

This project builds a team capable of performing real-time research and generating personalized outreach.

### Team Structure

1.  **Supervisor**: Manages the research and outreach process.
2.  **Lead Researcher**: Gathers up-to-date information about a specific person and their company.
3.  **Lead Sales Representative**: Uses the research report to draft personalized outreach messages.

### Enhancing Agents with Tools

> [!IMPORTANT]
> By default, LLMs cannot access live, up-to-date information. Equipping worker agents with **tools** solves this problem and extends their capabilities beyond their training data.

*   The **Google Custom Search** tool allows a worker agent to perform real-time web searches.
*   Flowise provides various tools, including a **Custom Tool** for bespoke integrations (e.g., calling APIs) and a **Calculator**.

> [!TIP]
> You can add multiple tools to a single worker. The agent will intelligently decide which tool is most appropriate to use for a given task.

### Dynamic Inputs with Prompt Variables

*   Use curly braces (e.g., `{lead_person}`) in your prompts to create dynamic variables.
*   Populate these variables at runtime using the **Format Prompt Values** feature on the worker node. This allows you to reuse the same agent team for different targets without changing the core prompts.

### Google Custom Search Tool Setup

To use the Google Search tool, you need two credentials:

1.  **Google Custom Search API Key**: Generated from the Google Cloud Console. You must create a project and enable the "Custom Search API" to get a key.
2.  **Programmable Search Engine ID**: Created by setting up a new search engine, configuring it to "search the entire web," and copying its ID.
transcription:
## Introducing Flowise Agentflows

Flowwise recently added a solution for creating AI agent teams without needing to write any code. You can simply add team members to the team by dragging and dropping nodes onto a canvas, and then providing the roles and responsibilities to each worker agent. The team members will then work together to solve the user's task.

This is similar to frameworks like Crew AI and AutoGen without the need to write any code yourself. In fact, Flowwise uses LangRoth under the hood. With an AI agent team, you can pass an instruction to a supervisor agent, and the supervisor will then delegate and orchestrate the tasks between the different team members.

In this video, we will have a look at learning the fundamentals of creating agent teams in Flowwise by creating two exciting projects. First, we will create our very own software development team, and second, we will create a lead research team that will make use of tools to achieve their task.

If you're new to Flowwise, then check out this video to set up Flowwise on your local machine. Also, if you don't see agent flows in the menu, then please ensure to update your Flowwise instance.

## Setting Up the Supervisor Agent

We can create our very first agent team by clicking on "Add New" within the Agent Flows page. Let's give our team a name by clicking on "Save", and let's call this "Software Development Team". Let's save this, and let's start by adding a supervisor to the canvas.

Within "Add Nodes", go to the multi-agent section, and add a supervisor. This supervisor agent is responsible for delegating the tasks between the different workers, and orchestrating the work until the task is achieved. The supervisor node takes in an LLM as input, and optionally we can also add input moderation. We can also give our supervisor a name, but I'll just leave it as "supervisor", and under additional parameters, we can see the system prompt for the supervisor, and we really don't have to change this. This prompt is simply telling the supervisor that it needs to manage the conversations between the different team members. We can go ahead and close out of this popup, and let's start by adding a chat model.

## Configuring the LLM and First Worker Agent

Under "Add Nodes", let's go to "Chat Models", and for this video, we're going to add the "Chat OpenAI Model", like so. Let's connect our chat model to the supervisor. Then within the "Chat OpenAI" node, let's select our credentials, and I've already set up my OpenAI credentials, but if you haven't done so already, simply click on "Create New", give your credential a name, and paste in your OpenAI API key. You can also check out this video, which shows you how you can create your OpenAI API key. Simply select your credentials from this drop-down, then under "Model Name", go ahead and select the new GPT40 model. Let's also change the temperature from 0.9 to 0.

Now we can start adding team members to this team. Let's go back to "Add Nodes", then under "Multi-Agents", let's add a "Worker" node. The "Worker" node can take in a list of tools as input, and we also need to assign a "Supervisor" node. So let's go ahead and attach our supervisor to this worker.

## Defining Worker Roles and Inheritance

We can also add a chat model to this node, and this is optional. If we don't attach a model to the worker itself, the worker will simply inherit the chat model that is being used by the supervisor node, so this OpenAI node over here. But if we wanted to override the model that is being used by this specific worker, we can simply attach a different chat model to this. This can be very useful for creating a team where different models need to verify each other's results. For this demo, we'll simply inherit the same chat model.

Let's give our worker a name. For this team, I actually want three workers. First, I want a product designer that is responsible for coming up with the feature set for our application. The second worker will be the software developer that is responsible for writing the code. And the third worker will be the technical writer which is responsible for writing the user manual for our application.

Let's start by creating our product designer. I will call this worker product designer, and for the worker prompt, we can specify the roles and responsibilities. Let's enter something like, "You work for a software development company. Your role as product designer is to come up with the features and product design based on the user requirements." Let's save this prompt, and let's have a look at the rest of the inputs on this node.

## Initial Test with One Worker Agent

We can also provide variables in this prompt template which we can then specify within the prompt values. And we will have a look at that in the second example. We can also specify the max iterations or leave it blank. This will simply tell the application how many times this node can go back and forth and make changes to its solution. Let's simply leave this blank. We can already test our team out by saving the chat flow. We can then click on this chat bubble. Let's expand this, and let's ask our team to build a to-do list app.

First, you will notice a message from the supervisor, and the supervisor is passing the request on to the product designer who is now currently busy with their task. And after a few seconds, we can see the response coming back from the product designer. Let's have a look at this. And the product designer did indeed list all the core features of our to-do list app. And this also includes some advanced features, the user interface design, the tech stack, and more.

## Building the Full Software Development Team

Now let's add our other two workers as well. So under add nodes, let's add another worker. Let's call this worker the developer. Let's attach our supervisor to our developer as well. And for the developer's prompt, let's enter something like, you work for a software development company. As an experienced software developer, you build software solutions using React, Next.js, Tailwind, CSS, Express, JavaScript, and Node. Let's save this, and let's also add our final worker, which is the technical document writer. So let's attach our supervisor to this node. Let's call this technical writer. And for the worker prompt, let's enter. You work for a software development company. Write a detailed user manual based on the product design and code written by the team members. The manual should be in markdown format. It's safe as prompt, and let's test our flow by saving it.

## Testing the Complete Software Team

And in the chat, let's expand this. Let's clear the chat, and let's ask it again, build a to-do list app. So we can see the supervisor passing the message to the product designer. What is impressive about this is the supervisor is able to correctly determine the sequence of events. It wouldn't make sense to ask the document writer or the developer to go first. So after we receive the product design, the supervisor now passes the product design over to the developer. The developer now put everything in place to build a software application, and it's also produced the code. We can now see the supervisor requesting the technical writer to write the user manual. And finally, we can see the manual that was produced by the technical writer. And this is in markdown format. Building an AI agent team couldn't be any easier.

## Starting the Lead Research Team Project

Now let's have a look at the second example, where we will build a lead research team that will be able to use tools. But first, if you like this video, hit the like button and subscribe to my channel. Also, let me know in the comments if there are any scenarios or use cases that you would like me to cover in a future video.

Let's go back to the dashboard and let's go to agent flows and let's create our second example. Let's save this. Let's call this lead outreach team and let's save this. Let's start by adding our supervisor. So we'll drag and drop the supervisor node. The supervisor also needs a chat model. So let's grab the chat open AI node. Let's attach the open AI node to the supervisor. Let's also select our credentials. Let's change the model to GPT40. And let's set the temperature to zero.

Now this team needs two workers. So let's go ahead and add those workers and I will explain what each of them will do. So let's add our first worker. Let's duplicate this and let's attach the supervisor to these two workers. So we'll do this and we'll attach it to this worker. Great. I'm going to clear the prompt templates for each of these. And let's give our first worker a name like lead researcher and for the second one, we'll call it the lead sales representative.

## Defining Roles and the Need for Tools

So what we want to do here is we want our researcher to go online and build out a detailed report of a specific lead. So effectively we want to tell this researcher to go online and build out a full report for a specific individual. This report needs to contain information like the professional experience, their involvement in projects and companies, etc. And the lead sales representative is then responsible for generating personalized messages based on the results from the researcher for that individual.

So one obvious issue here is that this researcher will have no way of going online and performing research. It will only be able to produce its report based on the data that it was trained on, which is not up to date and will not work in most instances. So what we'll do to solve this problem is to add a tool to this worker that will allow it to perform Google searches. And we will get back to that in a second. Let's first complete these prompts.

## Using Prompt Variables

So for the first worker, I'm actually going to paste in this prompt and feel free to pause the video to have a look at this prompt. But this is something that you could very easily generate with chat GPT. This is simply a role description for a lead research agent. And this is simply saying that this researcher needs to use all the tools available to it to build out a detailed report for a lead person working for a lead company. Let's save this and let's do the same for the sales representative. And this is simply telling this agent that is responsible for writing personalized messages for the lead person. So feel free to pause the video and have a look at this prompt. Again, your prompt does not have to be nearly as complicated as this, but this prompt does seem to work quite well. Let's save this.

And you might have noticed that in these prompts, we are using these curly braces and these represent variables, as we will be entering these variables by going to format prompt values. Within here, we can now swap out these values and I'm going to call my company Lion Research. Let's accept this.

## Testing the Team Without Search Tools

And for the lead person and company, we want to perform research for Harrison Chase, who works for Lang chain. So for the company, let's enter Lang chain. And for the person, let's enter Harrison Chase, like so. Let's close this pop up and let's do the same thing for the sales representative. Our company is called Lion Research. The lead company is called Lang chain. The lead person is called Harrison Chase. And for the lead activity, we will focus on the Lang graph. And as a reminder, this agent flow solution in Lang flow is actually based on the Lang graph framework that was developed by Lang chain. Let's close this. Let's save this flow. And we can go ahead and save this, although we haven't provided a tool for the researcher yet. And we will do that in a second. Let's just see if this is working so far by just typing go.

## Analyzing Pre-Tool Results and Integrating Google Search

Our supervisor is asking the researcher to write out that detailed report for our lead. And after the researcher is complete, the supervisor is now asking our sales representative to draft up those personalized messages. And we can indeed see those different messages being produced.

Now the issue here is this researcher produced this report based on the training data that is baked into the open AI models. This data could very much be outdated and inaccurate. We can greatly improve the results by giving this researcher access to a Google search tool. Let's do that now by going to add nodes and under tools, we can see a list of different tools that we can assign to any of these workers. For example, you could use a chat flow tool to allow the user to call any of your chat flows in flow wise, or you can use the custom tool to write your very own tools that could call service endpoints, for instance, to Zapier or make. But what we're interested in is this Google custom search tool.

Let's add this to the canvas and let's connect this tool to our worker. It's also useful to know that you can attach more than one tool to a worker. So as an example, let's add this calculator tool, we can take this tool and also attach it to the same worker and the worker will decide which tool to use and when.

## Configuring Google Custom Search Credentials

Right, so now to get this custom search tool working, we need to provide some credentials. Click on this drop down. And for you, there won't be any credentials yet. So click on create new, then give your credentials a name. I'll call this Google custom search YouTube tutorial, but you can call yours whatever you want. Then we need to provide a Google custom search API key, as well as a programmable search engine ID. These are very simple to set up.

First, let's go to the Google Cloud console. You will be asked to sign in with your Google account. Afterwards, you should see some sort of dashboard. Let's create a new project by clicking on this drop down and let's create a new project. Let's give our project a name. I'll call mine flow wise agent flow tutorial. Let's click on create. We can click on this drop down again. And then let's select the project that we just created. Now go to the navigation menu, then click on API and services, and then click on library. From the library, let's search for the custom search API. Click on the custom search API. And then lastly, click on enable. Once this has been enabled, click on credentials, then click on create credentials, and then API key. Let's copy this key and then back in flow wise, paste in that API key.

So let's go ahead and create our search engine ID. Let's click on this link and here simply enter the name of your search engine. I'll just call it flow wise agent flows. And then under this section, select search the entire web. And under search settings, I'm going to enable safe search. I'm also going to tell it that I'm not a robot and let's click on create. Now we can click on back to all search engines. We can then click on the search engine that we just created. And from here, we can find our search engine ID. Let's copy this. And now we can paste this into this field and let's click on add. Ensure that you've selected the credential that you just created and save your chat flow.

## Final Test with the Search-Enabled Team

So let's run this again. But this time we're expecting the researcher to use the Google custom search to perform its research. I'll just enter something like go. The supervisor is passing the instruction over to the researcher. Once the team has completed their work, let's go back up to the lead researcher. We can see that the lead researcher used the Google custom search tool four times. When we open up these tools, we can see the search query that was executed and the response from the Google results. And we can see that for each and every one of these tools. It is impressive to see how this researcher determined which search queries to use. And this time the results from the model is actually based on up to date information from Google.

I hope you enjoyed this video and I would like to know what use cases you would like me to cover in these tutorial videos. If you would like to learn everything there is to know about Flow-wise, then check out this tutorial series over here.
